internal_decisions: Added ABSOLUTE_ZERO_TOLERANCE_DECIMALS = 9 with a comment explaining why.
Single compiled regex with fullmatch; optional leading/trailing whitespace and a +/- sign are accepted.

addressed.problem: The tolerance used to compare with absolute zero is a bare literal 9 (decimal places) in the check, while the other thresholds (DECIMALS, ABSOLUTE_ZERO_C, KELVIN_OFFSET) are named constants.
addressed.fix: Add a named constant such as `ABSOLUTE_ZERO_TOLERANCE_DECIMALS = 9` and use it on line 34.
addressed.if_skipped: The reader cannot tell why 9 was chosen, and it is easy to change it without noticing the effect on the absolute-zero boundary.

plan: Baseline: unit tests (22) and acceptance tests (7) all pass.
Contracts: convert and parse tested from the consumer side. A parse→convert round trip is covered. The modules don't import each other.
Edge cases: absolute zero in C, K and F, just below zero, an unknown to_unit combined with a below-zero value, and malformed parse texts all behave as the contract says.
Defect tests test_d1, test_d2 and test_d3 in qa/test_qa_edges.py stay red on purpose (all low).
Run the QA tests with: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa
Discarded: regression, because the repo had no earlier behaviour beyond the version test. Security, performance and accessibility are not in the architecture and there is no risk surface.

defects.repro: convert(float('nan'), 'C', 'K') returns nan instead of raising ValueError.
defects.fix: Reject non-finite values with math.isfinite at the top of convert, or add that rule to the contract.
defects.if_skipped: NaN passes through the conversion and callers get a nan result.

defects.repro: convert(float('inf'), 'C', 'F') returns inf. convert(-inf, ...) raises, so the two infinities are handled inconsistently.
parse(None) raises TypeError from re. The contract says ValueError for anything else.
defects.fix: Check isinstance(text, str) and raise ValueError if it fails.
defects.if_skipped: Callers that catch only ValueError will crash on non-string input.

gaps: The architecture doesn't define behaviour for NaN, infinity or non-string input, so D1 to D3 are low and partly design questions.
Python 3.9 compatibility was not tested because only the local interpreter was available.

advisory.problem: AC-003: the tests never check the boundary. Exactly -273.15 C, 0 K and -459.67 F are valid inputs, so an implementation that rejects them (`<=` instead of `<`) would pass. The criterion says 'below absolute zero', so this boundary is part of it.
advisory.evidence: A check of `value_in_c <= -273.15` passes every current test. No test calls convert(-273.15, 'C', 'K') or convert(0, 'K', 'C') expecting a result, except test_ac_002, which does cover 0 K.

advisory.problem: AC-005: the invalid-text cases are only the four from the criterion. Other inputs the contract rejects (for example '12 C C', 'abc', or a space with no unit) are not tested.
advisory.evidence: A parser that handles only those four strings and returns a value for other garbage would pass.
